Resolves #20050

🌿 *The spec can no longer call the strip's own pre-drop pair a flash of the headers it withholds.*

`WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL`'s sampler now records the ids of the laid-out headers per frame, and the oracle asks the question the witness exists for: no frame lays out a header that the strip withheld both before the drop and once settled (the union of the pre-drop and settled visible sets is the allowed set; anything else is a withheld header painted, #19987's defect). The frame-count comparison against the settled count is gone, because the drop's focus restore reveals the strip's actions and re-partitions it to fewer headers, so the pre-drop pair legitimately stays laid out until that lands, a frame or more under load (gate-2 run 1's red on #20022, dispositioned there). The outside-the-box assertion and the sample-count floor stay. Spec-only; the product witness keeps its teeth.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium through the Neural Link fixture; the two diagonals below, run outside CI from a scratch spec that mirrors the drop and is not committed) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2); AC-3 outside CI; AC-4 in CI.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Outside CI: the same drop under `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 6×, five repeats, both oracles evaluated from one sample set: the old count rule fired in 1 of 5 (`before 2, settled 1, maxCount 2`, the gate-2 pattern), the identity rule produced no stray in 5 of 5. The AC is restated on #20050 to this paired-counterexample shape (N ≥ 5, old ≥ 1, identity 0); the earlier "3 of 3" was a target set before the measurement, not a receipt |
| AC-2 | Outside CI: a withheld header's id (`appliedHiddenIds[0]`) planted in the strip's DOM for one frame after the drop: the identity rule named it in 5 of 5 (two frames each) |
| AC-3 | Outside CI: the repaired file alone, `--repeat-each=3`, both arms: 6 of 6; no `waitForTimeout` added (`check-fixed-sleeps` runs in the pre-commit hook) |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: the hosted `e2e-brain` tier runs `WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL` on this head |
